title: Microsoft Copilot app: Chat suggests a better-fit mode such as Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, access rules, licensing and API calls are supported. Two minor corrections remain: finish the consumption-reporting path at Agents and services, and cite the API overview for the additional report types.

claims.where: title; front matter: products; What's changing
claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns mode handoffs in the Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot app mode handoffs

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Chat can suggest a better-fit mode after the user sends a prompt, where applicable.
claims.quote: The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable.

claims.claim: Cowork is the roadmap's example of a suggested mode.
claims.quote: For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans suggestions for other supported modes as they become available.
claims.quote: For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available.

claims.claim: The suggestion card explains the better-fit mode.
claims.quote: Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat, with an explanation of the better-fit mode and an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Switching to the suggested mode is the user's choice.
claims.quote: In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Chat conversation is attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context.
claims.quote: Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes the suggestion as a banner.
claims.quote: the user may see a banner suggesting that experience.

claims.claim: The banner offers the option to remain in Chat.
claims.quote: In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Accepting the switch opens the suggested experience with the prompt already sent.
claims.quote: If the user selects the option to switch, they will be brought directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent, along with the context from their Chat conversation attached.

claims.claim: Suggestions appear only for experiences the user can already access.
claims.quote: Users will see suggestions only for experiences they can access. For example, users who do not have access to Cowork will not see a suggestion to use Cowork.

claims.claim: The suggestion experience is on for its eligible audience without administrator action.
claims.quote: Only users who have the Copilot mode (example Cowork) enabled will see this experience. ... No admin action is required to prepare for this change.

claims.claim: Microsoft says no administrator action is required to prepare for this change.
claims.quote: No admin action is required to prepare for this change.

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The cited Message Center notice was updated on 13 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the Rollout schedule to reflect timing for Standard and Deferred audiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends considering informing users and the help desk about mode suggestions.
claims.quote: Consider informing your users and help desk that Copilot may suggest another Copilot mode when that mode may better fit a request or task.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users in scope of a spending policy selecting Cowork have Cowork access.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Removing Cowork access requires removing the user from every spending policy that includes Cowork.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not remove the Cowork access granted by a policy.
claims.quote: A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access. ... Setting a very low credit limit doesn't prevent access. A user can still open Cowork and start work until the limit is reached.

claims.claim: Configuration on the old Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents no longer controls who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is selected by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: With Auto-apply new services on, newly supported services and agents are added automatically.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: The Cowork policy route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Scope user and group > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration and select + Add spending policy. ... On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group. ... On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings/{serviceId} updates service access on a spending policy.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings/{serviceId} ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b/serviceSettings/cowork

claims.claim: The service-setting update request body sets the state property.
claims.quote: In the request body, supply the values for the properties to update. The state property can be updated.

claims.claim: The reference example uses serviceId cowork with state disabled.
claims.quote:
"serviceId": "cowork",
  "state": "disabled"

claims.claim: The group-scoped spending policy obtains its user scope from the selected groups.
claims.quote: To add specific users or resource accounts to a spending policy, ensure they're in a security group first and then select specific groups from the policy setup.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Spending limits are edited in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: ... Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} can update policy credit limits.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The policy update request body can set periodLimit.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The policy update request body can set perUserLimit.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption is the reporting surface for Cowork service consumption.
claims.quote: Select the Consumption tab. ... The Policies view is the default view ... In the Agents and services view, review usage for supported services. For example, Cowork and Work IQ API.
claims.fix: Complete controls[3].ui.path and the corresponding monitoring instruction as 'Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption > Agents and services'. The existing path reaches the correct page but stops before its Cowork service view.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageDetails/{userId}/services returns a user's consumption by service.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageDetails/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/services?startDateTime=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z&endDateTime=2026-07-02T00:00:00Z

claims.claim: The service-details operation splits one user's credit consumption by governed service for a timestamp window.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementUserUsageServiceDetail objects that split one user's raw consumption of Copilot Credits by governed service for a timestamp window.

claims.claim: Learn documents additional API usage reports by group, service and funding class.
claims.quote: usage reports that break down consumption by user, security group, governed service, and funding class.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/overview to sources for the existing statement about further reports by group, service and funding class.

claims.claim: Precedence among overlapping Cowork policies decides which limits apply, not whether access is granted.
claims.quote: When a user is in multiple policies that select Cowork, the precedence rules only choose which limits apply—they don't decide whether access is granted.

claims.claim: A more restrictive spending policy does not override a more permissive Cowork access policy.
claims.quote: Access is decided per service by whether any applicable policy selects that service. A more restrictive policy doesn't override a more permissive one.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft Graph cost management operations are beta APIs subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Cowork operates within the user's existing permissions and security boundaries.
claims.quote: It connects to your Outlook, Calendar, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and other Microsoft 365 services, operating within your existing permissions and security boundaries.

claims.claim: Cowork carries out multi-step tasks on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Cowork is an AI-powered agentic system that carries out multi-step tasks on your behalf across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Cowork tasks can send emails.
claims.quote: You describe what you need in natural language, and Cowork executes it—sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: Cowork tasks can schedule meetings.
claims.quote: You describe what you need in natural language, and Cowork executes it—sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: The Cowork application card says sensitive actions require the user's explicit approval before execution.
claims.quote: Each action is visible in the conversation, and sensitive actions require your explicit approval before they're executed.
